verdict.rationale: Greptile documents a versioned in-repo config file: greptile.json sits in the repo root, is read from the PR's source branch, and overrides dashboard settings. It covers review behavior, PR filters, file patterns, custom context, and repository-specific standards, and a strictness setting (1–3) gives coarse review tuning. Directory-scoped settings and rules are claimed on a marketing page but are not tied to greptile.json, and named review profiles are not documented, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: explicit per-path instructions documented in greptile.json, named review profiles (beyond a strictness level), full schema detail, independent or hands-on corroboration of the config file.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, I configure the reviewer with a versioned config file in my repo — path filters, per-path instructions, review profiles

citations.quote: Place `greptile.json` in your repository root. Settings are read from the source branch of the PR and override dashboard settings.
Control review behavior, PR filters, file patterns, custom context, and output formatting.
Scope review settings, rules, and context to the directories each team owns.
Control how strict Greptile is about leaving comments with the strictness setting (1–3).
